ai.description: *Minervarya andamanensis* is a small frog (25–35 mm) with a brown, warty dorsum and pale vertebral stripe. It features a distinct dark mask and prominent longitudinal skin ridges on the back.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya andamanensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent glandular fold running along the dorsolateral sides of its back.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya andamanensis* inhabits moist, lowland tropical forests and disturbed areas, often found near streams, marshes, or paddy fields within the Andaman Islands.
ai.behavior: The Andaman Wart Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the edges of forest streams and marshy habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya andamanensis* is an oviparous breeder that lays small clutches of eggs in stagnant water pools. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya andamanensis* is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring primarily in low-elevation forest habitats across the archipelago.
ai.callDescription: The Andaman Wart Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard calling from shallow, stagnant water in forest clearings.
